quest.title: A Forest of Change
quest.description: You and Paimon arrive in Sumeru, and you prepare to find a way to get an audience with Lesser Lord Kusanali...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Mora x25450, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark

talks.objective: Go to the Land of the Dendro Archon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that we've made it to Sumeru, our next objective should be to head to Sumeru City and find a way to meet with Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And speaking of Lesser Lord Kusanali, even though we haven't heard too much about her, she doesn't seem to be the same deity who abducted your {M#sister}{F#brother}...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But even so, people call Sumeru the "Nation of Wisdom," you know. If we can get a chance to meet the God of Wisdom, maybe she can give us some useful information.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, sounds like a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, uh... Paimon doesn't know the way to Sumeru City... Maybe we can climb up to that spot with the Statue of The Seven on it? That'll give us a way better view of things!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even if we can't see exactly where the city is, at least we'll be able to check for some smaller settlements nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second, look! There's someone up ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Perfect timing! Now we can just ask for directions rather than wander around like lost adventurers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there. Uh... we're not from around here and seem to have gotten a little lost... We'd like to ask for some directions!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Did they not hear Paimon? HEY! You over there! Could you give us some directions?

dialogues.speaker: Sumeru Local
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on here? There's no way she could've missed that... Wait! Could she be ignoring us!? How dare she?

choices.text: Calm down, it's probably nothing to get worked up about...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Well, even so, she might be heading someplace where we could find other people to ask. Let's keep our distance and follow her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When we get the chance, we'll just ask someone else for directions.

choices.text: Or maybe there's a reason she ignored us?

talks.objective: Observe the situation in the cave

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? She just walked near that small waterfall and then suddenly vanished! Let's go take a closer look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought this cave would lead to a village or something, but uh, it looks like that's not the case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, she's sitting over there. Wait, she couldn't possibly be living here, could she?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what should we do now? Do we try asking her for directions again?

choices.text: Sure, let's give it another shot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, it's not like we have anyone else we can ask... Even if she's not very friendly, we just need her to point us in the right direction, that's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Mmm! What a lovely smell!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's coming from that censer over there. This is definitely not your typical place to call home, but at least it smells nice! Hmm, maybe living here wouldn't be too bad after all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ugh! Uh oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, what's the matter? You don't look too good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Is the smell making you feel sick? Strange, Paimon doesn't feel anything...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I've got to get out of here!)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I think I'm gonna pass... out...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What's happening? {NICKNAME}? This is no time for a nap! C'mon, wake up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, it looks like she's meditating or something. If we bother her now, she probably wouldn't let us off very lightly...

talks.objective: Observe the situation in the cave

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Are you sure it's not serious? The Traveler's been out for a long time now...
#Yes, you can relax... Believe me, Master is extremely knowledgeable. If he says that {M#he}{F#she}'s going to be alright, then there's absolutely nothing to worry about.
Oh, are you awake now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, thank goodness! {NICKNAME}, you're finally awake!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where am I?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we're at... uh... Good question, where are we!? Paimon was in such a panic when you passed out that she even forgot to ask what place this is.
This is Gandharva Ville. It was originally built by scholars from Sumeru as a place to rest in the rainforest. Now it's mainly used by the Forest Rangers as a base of operations.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: My name is Collei. I'm a Trainee Forest Ranger. My master and I found you passed out during our patrol, so we brought you here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for the help.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh n—no, no thanks are necessary! I didn't do anything, really. By the way, how are you feeling now? Any discomfort?

choices.text: No, I seem to be fine, except...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, haha... That's Master's herbal medicine you're tasting. He gave you some while you were unconscious.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Before I forget, Master mentioned you should take more medicine once you wake up.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Ah, whoops!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Collei, what's the matter? Were you trying to retrieve the medicine? As I've already told you, you must be careful with these... I'll get it for you once I'm finished here.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Ah, sorry, Master...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: *sigh* Now, the "Guide to Avidya Forest's Edible Fungi" is clearly posted on our bulletin board. But, if Farbod forgets which mushrooms to avoid one more time, I'll have no choice but to leave the guide somewhere a little more visible — like right smack on his forehead so others can remind him to be careful.

response.speaker: Nasrin
response.text: Right, this is the second time he's come down with food poisoning this month. I'll be sure to give him a good talking-to!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Yes, please do. If, on the off-chance, Farbod simply enjoys having little imaginary fairies dance before his eyes, then we'll just let him be. But, the next time he requires any of our medicine, be sure to charge him accordingly.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: So, how are you doing? Feeling better?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, this is my master, Forest Watcher Tighnari. He is chief officer over all the rangers here in Gandharva Ville.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I already informed Paimon about the reason you fell unconscious earlier, but now that you're awake, let me explain it for you as well.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It is common practice for Sumeru scholars of certain Darshans to dedicate themselves to training and meditation in isolated areas, particularly the nearby forests. While meditating, they use a certain incense known as Spirit Borneol to help calm their minds as they enter a state of deep rumination.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: In hopes of asking directions, you two followed a scholar named Haypasia into her cave. The incense you smelled inside was the Spirit Borneol I just mentioned.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That incense typically has no effect on most people. But, for a very select few, it can have profound effects on one's cognition, as you experienced firsthand. Does that make sense?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, that all makes sense.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Very good. Now, answer me this, did you feel anything after passing out? Say, any out-of-body experiences, or did you see anything while unconscious?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe what you saw while unconscious...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Collei, let the others know to stop bringing their patrol logs here for now.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Huh? Wh—Why?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Because {M#these two}{F#these two} will be staying here for the next few days. They can have my room, and I'll bunk with Amir. Now get a move on and be sure to do as I've said.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Uh, yes, Master Tighnari!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, hold on a second! Can you tell us what's going on?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Sure, let me fill you in. I originally planned to send you on your way once you finished your medicine. However, it appears now that you should stay a while longer in Gandharva Ville for further observation while you recuperate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Further observation?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But we need to get to Sumeru City...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: No need to be hasty. As long as you have the capacity to judge between right and wrong, I promise that you'll understand the gravity of the situation once I explain everything to you.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Based on what you saw after smelling the incense and losing consciousness, we can conclude that you experienced a powerful hallucination, which suggests your mental state is not in the best of shape.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: If you're skeptical, have a whiff of this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wha—!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, are you okay?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: You're experiencing a similar sensation as when you passed out, aren't you?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: So even though your condition is stable as of now, if I were to haphazardly let you leave, it's highly likely that you'd suddenly pass out again somewhere else.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The rainforest is home to many fierce animals and hazardous areas. If something were to happen to you again, I'm afraid you might not be so lucky.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: For now, I suggest you continue taking your medicine each day and avoid wandering off on your own, at least until you stop having adverse reactions to this kind of smell, okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Mmm, good. Now continue resting while I fire up another bowl of medicine for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Seriously, we just arrived in Sumeru. We're already having problems left and right...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows we were set on meeting Lesser Lord Kusanali as soon as possible, but you really don't look too good... It'd probably be best to let you recover first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, hey! Are you even listening to Paimon? Paimon's over here worrying about you, ya know!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I feel it's a little weird...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's weird? You mean how you're feeling now?

choices.text: Yeah, my body does feel a little weird, but what I mean is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean the vision of tree roots and red skies you saw? But if those weren't hallucinations, what could they be?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not sure.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (When I saw the vision, it felt as if I was standing deep underground. But the red sky... Could it have been Khaenri'ah?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, considering how unique you are, Paimon trusts your judgment here. But why didn't you say anything about it to Tighnari?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he misjudged your condition, then there's a chance you could get worse, right?

choices.text: I don't think that's the case.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You mean that Tighnari already knows that what you saw weren't hallucinations? But if that's the case, why would he try to hide that from us?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Exactly. We need to get to the bottom of this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it now... That explains why you were so quiet earlier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that settles it, then. We'll stay here to rest up and figure out what's going on with your hallucinations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it seems like asking Tighnari might not be an option anymore... What do you think we should do?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's start by having a chat with Collei.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea. Collei's pretty friendly... We can ask her tomorrow about what she knows regarding the Dendro Archon and customs in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You get a night of rest...

choices.text: He probably wasn't telling us the truth.
I don't think what I saw were hallucinations.
This taste in my mouth... It's so bitter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's follow her. Just keep quiet and make sure she doesn't notice us.
